> 齧缺問於王倪，四問而四不知。齧缺因躍而大喜，行以告蒲衣子。

Four questions, four "I don't know." The student jumps up delighted and goes to tell someone else.

## 應 does not mean "ought"

The title is usually read as a manual: how a ruler should govern. That reading is a mistranslation of the first character, and it turns the chapter into the exact thing it is dismantling.

應: to answer, to respond to what has come. 感而後應 — there is a thing first, then a response. Before the response there is no prepared plan.

So 應帝王 is not "the emperor ought to." It is: whoever sits in that seat, how do they answer? The answer is in the character: respond, do not originate.

Read it as "ought" and you get a list of virtues for rulers. 莊子 is taking apart the list.

## 非人, and an honest disagreement

非人 appears twice in the chapter, and the commentaries split. One reading: 非人 is the realm of human-made division — ritual, law, calculation — so 有虞氏未始出於非人 means he never left that realm. The other reading, following 郭象: 非人 means "things," and the line means he never stopped treating things as things.

The two readings agree on the verdict — 有虞氏 does not reach 泰氏 — and differ only on how to name what 泰氏 holds. The book takes the first.

This is worth showing because it is how the book works: the disagreement is recorded, not smoothed.

## Three 機

壺子 shows a visitor three states in sequence: 杜德機, closed, still as earth; 善者機, the vital motion appearing, quiet with life in it; 衡氣機, the balance with no end favored.

The point is not that the third is best. The point is that a person who can be read is a person who has a fixed state, and a fixed state can be handled by anyone who knows it.

## 用心若鏡

The mirror does not welcome, does not send off. It reflects what arrives and keeps nothing after it leaves.

This is the chapter's operational instruction, and it is almost embarrassingly plain: respond to what is in front of you, do not store it.

## 渾沌: the last image of the inner seven

渾沌 has no seven apertures. Two visitors, meaning well, decide to bore them for him — one a day, seven days — and on the seventh day 渾沌 dies.

The parable is usually read as "do not interfere." That is too soft. What kills 渾沌 is not malice; it is the assumption that a complete thing is missing something, plus the goodwill to supply it.

The visitors are not villains. They are helpers. That is why the image closes the inner seven rather than a chapter on politics: the deepest form of 合 — the manufactured join — is the improvement offered by someone who is sure you are incomplete.

## The test

Where are you answering with a plan you prepared before the situation arrived? And where are you boring apertures into something that was already whole — a person, a team, a practice — because you can see what it lacks?
